reasons: No test for the confidence figure's mismatch display, the run stamp, or the evidenced share is visible in the packet.
Formula labels are typed by hand and would not change if the engine formula changed.
Only the evidence chip has tests in the packet.

terms.meaning: How well a claim is backed: grounded in evidence, a declared prerequisite, or unsupported.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Explains the shared visual pieces
sections.what: The header comment introduces the shared pieces: the evidence chip, the confidence figure and the run stamp, and says what each is for. The file imports the types and helpers those pieces need.
sections.why: The comment explains that these pieces carry the central argument: which claims are evidenced and how sure the viewer is.
sections.watch_out: The file imports many helpers from other modules. If one of them changes its name, every view that uses these pieces breaks.

sections.name: STANDING_MARK
sections.title: Maps standing to symbols
sections.what: Gives each standing value a short bracketed symbol, shown beside the word.
sections.why: The mark, word and colour together keep the standing readable in greyscale and to screen readers.
sections.watch_out: If a new standing value is added without a symbol, the chip shows nothing in that position.

sections.name: Field
sections.title: Labelled value row
sections.what: Shows a label and a value side by side with classes for styling.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond layout.

sections.name: Section
sections.title: Titled block with optional note
sections.what: Wraps content in a titled section, with an optional note line under the title.
sections.why: Gives every view the same heading and note pattern.

sections.name: EvidenceChip (part 1)
sections.title: Decides and corrects evidence standing
sections.what: Looks up which cited ids exist in the evidence lookup. If none exist but some were cited, the claim is marked unsupported and the summary counts the fabricated citations. It also builds the warning text for missing citations.
sections.why: The comment says a claim with only missing ids used to show as green grounded evidence. A fabricated citation is treated as worse than a missing one, so the warning is raised outside the closed panel.
sections.watch_out: The standing passed in by callers only reads the id list. This correction is what checks the ids, so removing it would bring back the false green.

sections.name: EvidenceChip (part 2)
sections.title: Renders the clickable evidence chip
sections.what: Draws a button showing the mark, the standing word and the count. It also shows the dangling citation warning, the wave edge note and the cost note outside the panel. The panel, when opened, lists the evidence cards, or explains that the claim cites nothing or only fabricated ids.
sections.why: The warning sits outside the panel so a reader sees it without clicking. The open state is kept only in memory.
sections.watch_out: The panel starts closed, so anything placed only inside it is easy to miss.

sections.name: EvidenceCard
sections.title: Shows one piece of evidence
sections.what: Displays one evidence item with its id, store name, authority label, publication date, excerpt and source reference.
sections.why: Gives the reader the source behind each claim.
sections.watch_out: If a field is dropped from the data type, it silently disappears from this card.

sections.name: ConfidenceFigure (part 1)
sections.title: Shows confidence as its parts
sections.what: Builds a table that lists citations and gaps, coverage, recency, agreement and the product. The product is recomputed from stored features. If agreement was not measured, that row is labelled not measured and left out of the product. If the recomputed value differs from the stored one, a warning is shown.
sections.why: The comment says confidence is never shown as a single bare score. Agreement is left out instead of being filled with a guess.
sections.watch_out: The formula labels are written out as text. If the engine's formula changes, these labels must change too.

sections.name: ConfidenceFigure (part 2)
sections.title: Warns when stored score does not match
sections.what: When the recomputed score and the stored score disagree, shows a message saying one of them is wrong and that the difference is shown rather than hidden.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the message itself. Likely reason: a disagreement is a finding the reader should see.

sections.name: RunStamp
sections.title: Shows depth tier and model versions
sections.what: Prints the depth tier, schema version, run id and classification, the number of agents, the distinct model ids, and a bold warning that bands from different schema versions cannot be compared. The warning value is computed from a constant in the bands module.
sections.why: The comment says the depth tier and model ids must appear on every page, and the schema warning is shown here instead of in a footnote so it appears on every printed page.
sections.watch_out: The comparability note is computed from the bands constant, so changing that constant changes this text too.

sections.name: WarningBanner
sections.title: Status box for warnings
sections.what: A simple box that holds warning text and is announced as a status message.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the status role. Likely reason: screen readers announce status messages.

sections.name: EvidencedShare
sections.title: Shows the share of value that is evidenced
sections.what: Shows the evidenced percentage and the hypothesis percentage for a scope label. When the share is exactly zero, it adds a no-evidence prefix and a special style.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: readers should see how much of the total rests on stated assumptions.
sections.watch_out: The check uses exact zero, so a tiny positive share will not show the warning.

summary: Shared visual building blocks used by all views: evidence chips and cards, confidence breakdowns, the run stamp, warning boxes and the evidenced share line.
purpose: Makes the viewer's key claims visible and hard to misread. Evidence standing, confidence arithmetic, run depth and comparability warnings all appear here.
why: The header comment explains the three main pieces: standing is shown as a mark, a word and a colour so it survives printing and colour blindness; confidence is never shown as a bare score; and the run stamp appears on every page.
how: Each component takes plain data, such as a list of evidence ids or a confidence block, and returns markup. The evidence chip checks which ids resolve in the evidence lookup and corrects the standing when every citation is missing. The confidence figure recomputes the score from its features and shows a warning if the stored score differs. The run stamp reads the manifest and prints the depth tier, run id and model ids.
inputs: Evidence ids and their standing, a lookup of known evidence, confidence blocks, the run manifest, and share percentages with a scope label.
outputs: Rendered markup for each piece. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere.
risks: If a field is removed from a shared data type, its citation silently disappears from the screen. The confidence formula is typed out in text here, so it can drift from the engine. The no-evidence warning appears only when the share is exactly zero.
debug: If a citation looks wrong, check the evidence lookup and the chip's correction logic. If a confidence figure shows a mismatch, compare the stored score with the recomputed score and check the features. If the run stamp is wrong, check the manifest file. Run the evidence chip tests after any change here.
